# `geoclaw_tsunami_inundation`

A TSUNAMI from a sea-floor rupture across the open sea to a coast, and how far inland and how deep it floods, with the wave's arrival time and the water level at a gauge.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| module | `geoclaw` - 159 keywords in its dictionary, of which this template states 35 |
| solves | `trid3nt_server.workflows.geoclaw.engine.solve_case` |
| engine defaults | every keyword this template does not state keeps the engine's own default; `describe_keywords` names it with that default, and `keywords={...}` sets it |

## The data it consumes

| row | produced by | what it is | datum |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extent` | supplied by the caller | a layer you supply, as a uri or a layer name; required - the template names no source for it. | - |
| `source` | supplied by the caller | a layer you supply, as a uri or a layer name; required - the template names no source for it. | - |
| `approach` | supplied by the caller | a layer you supply, as a uri or a layer name; required - the template names no source for it. | - |
| `domain` | supplied by the caller | the closed polygon this run solves over, as a uri, a layer name or a drawn shape. | - |
| `bed` | matched on a need for bathymetry | what the domain's nodes carry for elevation: a DEM, a bathymetry or survey raster, a layer of soundings, or a depth in metres below the free surface; unfilled, the run matches a source of bathymetry. | - |

## The inputs

The values the template declares. `desc` is what the model reads when it fills one.

| input | units | default | desc |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed` | - | optional | A point on the water off the coast: where the vertical datum offsets are measured and where the gauge stands, as a Point; the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair or 'lat,lon'. An offset of a tidal datum exists at the water only, and the point is never moved. |
| `level1_cell_m` | m | 7421.333333333333 | The level-1 cell edge along a meridian, in metres; the tutorial's 4 arcminutes. The user's lever for how coarse the open sea is, and nothing refuses one. |
| `deep_bed` | - | optional | The coarse surface under the fine bed, over the whole grid: a raster or a layer name on the run's vertical frame; unstated, ETOPO 2022 is fetched over the grid. |
| `initial_surface` | - | optional | A water surface the run opens at, as a raster of surface elevation on the run's vertical frame: a source stated by the sea surface it raises, beside the sea-floor rupture; unstated, the sea opens flat. |
| `event_time` | - | optional | The moment the scenario is read at - an ISO date or datetime (YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), from phrasing like 'during last Tuesday's storm'. Each source keeps its own retention, and a request deeper than one refuses typed |
| `module` | - | optional | The GeoClaw module the run solves: 'geoclaw' (shallow water) or 'geoclaw_bouss' (the Boussinesq SGN / Madsen-Sorensen equations, the same keywords plus Clawpack's BOUSS_ ones); unstated, the template's own. |
| `cores` | - | optional | The MPI process count the Boussinesq executable runs under (PETSc's linear solves use them); a whole number from 1 to this box's cores, unstated 1. Shallow-water runs take none. |
| `threads` | - | optional | The OpenMP thread count of each process of the Boussinesq executable (OMP_NUM_THREADS); a whole number from 1 to this box's cores, unstated the executable's own default (every core per process, so several processes oversubscribe the box). Shallow-water runs take none. |
| `vertical_frame` | - | NAVD88 | Vertical datum the bed's elevations are counted from, and with them the level over it. A source published on another frame reaches this one through a measured offset, and a pair nobody publishes an offset between refuses by name |
